title: Finite hypercovers compute derived sections with Grothendieck coefficients
statement: Let X be qcqs, A a Grothendieck abelian category and q a natural number. The q-th classical right-derived functor of evaluation of A-valued small-etale sheaves at the explicit identity etale object id_X satisfies IsCohomologyColimit A q: homotopic refinements give equal maps, the canonical cohomology comparisons commute with refinements, and every refinement-compatible family to an object B factors uniquely through this right-derived section object.

source.place: Detailed proof, paragraph 1: identification of hypercover cohomology with right-derived global sections

proof.text: Use the canonical comparison cocone. In degree zero its mediator is already proved invertible; in positive degree apply the finite-refinement colimit theorem.

Transfer the colimit universal property across the mediator isomorphism. The chosen terminal etale object and the explicit identity object give naturally isomorphic section functors; apply rightDerived to this natural isomorphism and transport the cocone.

Homotopy invariance is supplied by the concrete model. For each compatible family construct a quotient-indexed cocone by quotient induction, then use the transported colimit mediator and uniqueness to give the required unique factorization.

proof_origin.place: Detailed proof, paragraph 1: identification of hypercover cohomology with right-derived global sections; generalization from abelian groups to Grothendieck abelian coefficients using the categorical constructions described in the proof. The cited Stacks result itself is for abelian sheaves.

lean.statement:
theorem isCohomologyColimit_rightDerived_sections
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] (q : ℕ) :
    IsCohomologyColimit A q
      ((sheafToPresheaf X.smallEtaleTopology A ⋙
        (evaluation X.Etaleᵒᵖ A).obj
          (op (MorphismProperty.Over.mk ⊤ (𝟙 X)
            (MorphismProperty.id_mem _ X)))).rightDerived q)
